correctness.rationale: Every B_n is an exact deletion subsequence of B_k repeated 2^(n-k) times; the deleted count is 2^(n-k)(k+1)-(n+1). Every deletion can affect at most t-1 source-span counts of length-t output windows. Phase, gap-deletion count, and mask reconstruct each block, yielding H_mu(t)<=log2(length(B_k))+G((t-1)q_k)+F_t((t-1)q_k). The geometric maximum-entropy bound, concavity of log binomial coefficients and chosen k yield log2(t+2)+2log2(log2(t+2)+2)+7. The factor-frequency convergence and positivity inputs are also reconstructed, and the finite checker has 3430 passing tests. Computation is not used to establish the infinite bound.

value.rationale: The word has golden-mean language with exponential factor count and a full-support canonical measure; quantifying that measure’s Shannon information as at most log2(t)+2log2log2(t)+O(1) exhibits a strong and motivated topological-vs-statistical complexity separation. The deletion-mask entropy method is structurally nontrivial and potentially reusable for other near-doubling constructions. A constant-step textbook deduction from factor-count results cannot yield this estimate.
